packages.label: הַלֵּב וְהָאֱלֹקוּת — הָאֵין סוֹף שֶׁבִּפְנִים
packages.label_en: The Heart and Divinity — The Inner Infinity
packages.reason: The teaching's central structural insight is that the heart (לב) and the brain/mind (מוח) are parallel expressions of the same inner capacity — together they form the faculty that contains infinite reality. The teaching then grounds this infinite capacity in a single cause: Divinity (אלקות). Line 4 states explicitly: 'וְזֶה רַק מֵחֲמַת שֶׁנִּמְצָא שָׁם הָאֱלֹקוּת' — 'and this is only because the Divinity is found there.' This is an essence statement: the heart's unbounded capacity IS Divinity; Divinity IS what the heart essentially contains. Line 5 deepens this: 'אִם בְּהַלֵּב, שֶׁנִּמְצָא שָׁם רַק בְּחִינוֹת אֱלֹקוּת' — 'if in the heart, where there are only aspects of Divinity (bechinot elokut)' — using the explicit bechina-formula word 'בְּחִינוֹת', declaring the heart's contents to be aspects/dimensions of Divinity. The heart (לב) and the mind/brain (מוח) are treated throughout the teaching as a single inner faculty — lines 3 and 4 link them together structurally as the small physical vessel that contains the infinite. They are not presented as cause and effect (the brain does not produce the heart, nor vice versa); they are co-expressions of the same inner spiritual faculty. Similarly, the 'heart of kings' (לב מלכים) cited from Proverbs 25 is used as the paradigm of this infinite inner capacity — it is the same thing as 'לב' (the heart of anyone who has Divinity in it). The אין חקר (unsearchability/infinity) is not something the heart produces — it IS the heart's essential nature, stated three times in the text as an identity ('לב מלכים אין חקר'). All four nodes — לב, מוח, אלקות, and לב מלכים/אין חקר — are parallel aspects of the same spiritual reality: the infinite inner capacity rooted in Divinity's presence within the human person. Polarity is unambiguously good: this package describes the domain of holiness, Divinity, and the soul's boundless capacity for spiritual reality.

לב and מוח: Lines 3-4 treat heart and brain as a single inner faculty that together 'contain everything' (תּוֹפְסִים הַכֹּל). They are described in the same breath: 'הַלֵּב וְהַמֹּחַ שֶׁקְּטַנִּים מְאֹד בִּמְקוֹמָם, הֵם תּוֹפְסִים הַכֹּל'. They are not cause and effect (the brain does not cause the heart's capacity); they are co-expressions of the same capacity — both small physically, both infinite in spiritual content. The bechina is symmetric: heart = mind as the inner faculty of containing.

לב and אלקות: Line 4 states 'וְזֶה רַק מֵחֲמַת שֶׁנִּמְצָא שָׁם הָאֱלֹקוּת' — the heart's infinite capacity IS Divinity's presence. Line 5 uses 'בְּחִינוֹת אֱלֹקוּת' explicitly — the heart contains 'aspects of Divinity.' The heart's essential nature is to be the vessel/expression of Divinity; Divinity's essential presence in the human being IS the heart. This is a genuine bechina, not an eitza: Divinity does not produce the heart's capacity as a separate downstream effect — Divinity IS the heart's inner nature.

לב and לב מלכים: The teaching uses 'לב מלכים אין חקר' (Proverbs 25) three times as the definitive characterization of the heart's infinite nature. The verse is not cited as a cause that produces the heart's capacity — it IS the identity statement: the heart of kings IS unsearchable, meaning the heart's essential quality IS אין חקר (infinity/unsearchability). 'לב מלכים' is the paradigmatic expression of 'לב' — both refer to the same inner faculty, with 'מלכים' (kings) representing those who fully actualize the heart's infinite capacity (as line 8 explains: the king's greatness is entirely in the heart's knowledge of its dominion).

No evil mirror: Torah #191 does not develop an explicit evil counterpart. The teaching presents the contrast between the צדיק whose heart is full (all 310 worlds, all pleasures) and the person whose heart is empty (sits next to him but feels nothing). However, this contrast is expressed through the eitza/narrative structure of the teaching — it is not developed into a named bechina cluster for the evil domain. The empty-hearted person is not given a set of parallel bechina concepts; he is simply the negative case used to highlight the positive reality. Consistent with other short aphoristic teachings in LM that present the positive ideal without structuring the negative into a separate bechina family.

packages.label: עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְשַׁ"י עוֹלָמוֹת — הַתַּעֲנוּגִים שֶׁבַּלֵּב
packages.label_en: The World to Come and 310 Worlds — The Inner Pleasures
packages.reason: The teaching's opening and closing frame the same cluster of concepts: תענוגים ושעשועים (pleasures and delights), שי"ט עולמות (310 worlds), and עולם הבא (World to Come). These are presented as parallel expressions of the same spiritual reality — not as cause-and-effect stages. Line 1 introduces them as a single unit: 'כָּל הַתַּעֲנוּגִים וְהַשַּׁעֲשׁוּעִים וְכָל הַשַּׁ"י עוֹלָמוֹת' — pleasures, delights, and 310 worlds are listed together as the content of the full heart. Line 10 closes with the definitive identity statement: 'עִקַּר הַרְגָּשַׁת תַּעֲנוּג וְשַׁעֲשוּעַ עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכָל הַשַּׁ"י עוֹלָמוֹת – הַכֹּל הוּא בַּלֵּב' — 'the essential feeling of pleasure and delight of the World to Come and all the 310 worlds — all of it is in the heart.' This is an explicit identity/bechina statement: the World to Come IS what is experienced as pleasure in the heart; the 310 worlds ARE the pleasures and delights. They do not produce one another sequentially — they are three names for the same spiritual content that fills the heart of the tzaddik. The dominant node is עולם הבא because it is the eschatological frame (what awaits the righteous) and because the teaching's apex statement ('אַשְׁרֵי לוֹ' — praiseworthy is he) concludes by identifying עולם הבא as the content of the full heart. Polarity is good: these are entirely positive concepts belonging to the domain of holiness, the righteous, and spiritual reward.

תענוגים ושעשועים and שי"ט עולמות: Listed together four times in the text (lines 1, 9, 10 and implicitly in line 5 'עוֹלָמוֹת אֵין מִסְפָּר'). They are not cause and effect — they co-describe the same reality. The '310 worlds' (שי"ט עולמות — from the gematria of the word שי"ט) is a Kabbalistic idiom for the complete spiritual inheritance of the righteous; 'pleasures and delights' is the experiential descriptor of that inheritance. They are two faces of the same spiritual content.

עולם הבא and תענוגים ושעשועים: Line 10 explicitly equates them: 'עִקַּר הַרְגָּשַׁת תַּעֲנוּג וְשַׁעֲשוּעַ עוֹלָם הַבָּא' — 'the essential feeling of pleasure and delight of the World to Come.' The World to Come IS essentially experienced as pleasure and delight; pleasure and delight IS the experiential essence of the World to Come. Neither produces the other — they are the same reality described from different angles.

Connection to Package 1: Packages 1 and 2 are connected through the node לב (the heart). Package 1 describes what the heart IS (Divinity, infinite capacity); Package 2 describes what the heart CONTAINS (the pleasures/310 worlds/World to Come). The flow between them is eitza: the heart's infinite capacity (Package 1) enables the possession of all the pleasures and worlds (Package 2). This is a cross-package eitza, not a within-package bechina — correctly keeping the two packages separate.

The teaching presents the contrast between the tzaddik (full heart) and the empty-hearted person, but the empty-hearted person is not given his own named bechina cluster. The contrast operates as a narrative frame (eitza/consequence) rather than a structural bechina family. stats.eitza_summary: The causal structure of Torah #191: the presence of Divinity in the heart (Package 1) —eitza→ the ability to hold 310 worlds and all pleasures (Package 2). A kal va-chomer (a fortiori) reasoning structure appears in lines 6-7: if even a non-Jewish king's heart can contain his entire kingdom, how much more so can one reason upward to the Creator's infinite greatness. Line 8 states the result: the king's greatness, pleasure, and dominion are in the heart-knowledge. The cross-package eitza: Package 1 (heart = Divinity = infinity) —eitza→ Package 2 (heart contains 310 worlds/World to Come/pleasures). The tzaddik (צדיק, mentioned in line 9) is an eitza-node — the person who actualizes this potential and has all the worlds in his heart — but is not given a bechina equation in the text that would make him a bechina-family member of either package.
stats.teaching_structure: Torah #191 is a ten-sentence philosophical meditation. Structure: (1) Opening paradox — two people sit next to each other in Gan Eden, one feels all pleasures, the other feels nothing [sets up the puzzle]; (2) The proof from Proverbs 25 and the Talmudic saying — the heart of kings is unsearchable, exceeding even the infinite heavens; (3) The heart and brain together contain all provinces and heavenly qualities; (4) The reason: Divinity is in the heart; (5) The a-fortiori: if even partial Divinity gives the heart such capacity, how vast is the capacity; (6) Even for non-Jews, the heart of a king contains his entire kingdom; (7) Kal va-chomer: estimate God's greatness by the same logic; (8) Conclusion about the king: his greatness is only in the heart-knowledge; (9) Application back to opening paradox: the tzaddik has all 310 worlds in his heart; the neighbor's heart lacks it; (10) Beatitude and closing identity statement: all the pleasures, the World to Come, and 310 worlds are in the heart.
